meta.title: KB Labs — AI Control Plane for Developers
meta.description: Self-hosted workflows, agents, and plugins. Run AI automation on your own infrastructure with full control.

ctaSection.title: Run it on one real workflow.
ctaSection.description: One command. Runs on your machine. First workflow live in under an hour.

workflowSection.title: Define once. Run anywhere. Trace everything.
workflowSection.description: Releases, reviews, QA gates, AI agents — all described as code, running on one engine. Version them in git, run them from CLI or CI, inspect every step.

trustSection.subtitle: Releases, code review, commit policy, QA gates, dependency management — all running as plugins on the same engine you'll install.
trustSection.quote: I build on KB Labs every day. Every release, every review gate, every QA check. It's the same engine you install.
trustSection.stat1Desc: No cloud dependency in the core path
trustSection.stat3Desc: From install to a working workflow

integrationsSection.title: 21+ adapters. Swap any vendor in config.
integrationsSection.subtitle: Every external dependency — LLM, database, vector store, cache, storage — is behind a typed contract. Change the implementation without touching your code.

items.question: We already have a full stack. Do we need to migrate?
items.answer: No. KB Labs is designed to sit beside what you already run. Install it, connect one workflow, and keep everything else untouched. You grow the surface area when it makes sense for your team — never because the tool asked you to.

items.question: Is it free? Will it stay free?
items.answer: The OSS core is free and will stay free. It's the engine, and the engine doesn't close. A commercial support layer is on the roadmap for teams that need guarantees — SLA, dedicated support, advanced governance — but it's additive, never a gate in front of the core.

items.question: I work alone, or with a tiny team. Is this still for me?
items.answer: Especially for you. KB Labs is built on the idea that a person plus agents is a team. A plugin-agent can run your reviews. An external agent like Claude or Codex can drive your workflows through the same contracts. You stay in control of what they're allowed to do. Solo builders with agents get the most value from this from day one.

items.question: How does KB Labs treat humans, agents, and bots?
items.answer: The same way. KB Labs is a runtime with one permissions model, one observability surface, and one extension contract — applied equally to any kind of runner. A human running a workflow, an internal plugin-agent, an external agent, a CI bot — they all declare what they're allowed to do and the runtime enforces it. No one gets privileges. No one escapes the rails. MCP is on the roadmap as the next protocol-level extension of this.

items.question: How long does on-prem setup actually take?
items.answer: One command installs the launcher. A working environment with your first workflow is typically ready within an hour. No cloud dependency, no provisioning ceremony.

items.question: We already have CI/CD. Why not just extend that?
items.answer: CI/CD is great at build and deploy. KB Labs is for everything around it — commit policy, AI review gates, QA trend tracking, release coordination, agent workflows. Things that don't belong in a pipeline YAML and don't scale as config.

agentsSection.title: Agent calls the command. Not your key.
agentsSection.para1Start: Write a plugin — the agent gets a set of commands. Keys, access rights, audit — inside the plugin. The agent doesn't know how GitHub works — it just calls
agentsSection.para2: KB Labs native agents go further — every step is traced, analytics calculated automatically, nothing is lost.
